metadata.project: Deterministic Finite Automaton (DFA) for Smart-Home Energy Automation Controllers

scenarios.title: Nominal Power Dispatch Cycle
scenarios.description: System starts in IDLE, powers up into NORMAL_OPERATION, and steadily balances standard household load.
scenarios.academic_justification: All transitions remain within nominal operational parameters. Final state q1 ∈ F.

scenarios.title: Renewable Solar Prioritization & Dusk Return
scenarios.description: System detects rooftop solar availability, switches to green priority mode, sustains solar generation, and returns to normal grid power at sunset.
scenarios.academic_justification: DFA moves from q0 to q1, switches to eco mode q2 upon solar detection, self-loops in q2, then transitions to q1 when solar generation ceases. q1 ∈ F.

scenarios.title: Peak Consumption Surge & Load Shedding
scenarios.description: Power demand exceeds configured grid limit, triggering demand response (ENERGY_SAVING). Sustained high demand maintains conservation before returning to normal.
scenarios.academic_justification: System throttles non-essential loads by transitioning δ(q1, H) = q3, remains in q3, and restores δ(q3, N) = q1 when demand normalizes. q1 ∈ F.

scenarios.title: Storage Battery Depletion & Solar Replenishment
scenarios.description: During solar operation, battery storage drops below 25%, causing the controller to enter ENERGY_SAVING until strong solar generation alleviates the deficit.
scenarios.academic_justification: Low battery event forces conservation δ(q2, B) = q3. Re-emergence of solar irradiance restores green eco-mode δ(q3, S) = q2. q2 ∈ F.

scenarios.title: Critical Safety Fault Trip & Lockout Latching
scenarios.description: A thermal overload / electrical fault occurs during solar operation. System enters SAFETY_SHUTDOWN and ignores subsequent solar or demand events.
scenarios.academic_justification: SAFETY_ALERT trips controller into q4. The latch invariant ensures δ(q4, N)=q4 and δ(q4, H)=q4. Final state q4 ∉ F results in sequence rejection.

scenarios.title: Supervised Reset & Controlled Restoration
scenarios.description: Following an emergency trip, an authorized technician inspects hardware and issues a supervised RESET, returning controller to IDLE before nominal startup.
scenarios.academic_justification: The only permissible exit vector from q4 is RESET, taking the machine to q0 (standby), preventing accidental re-energization. Subsequent NORMAL brings it safely to q1 ∈ F.

scenarios.title: Repeated Identical Event Bursts (Idempotency)
scenarios.description: Consecutive bursts of HIGH_DEMAND and SOLAR_AVAILABLE test deterministic self-loop stability without state oscillations.
scenarios.academic_justification: DFA exhibits idempotency: δ(q3, H)=q3 for repeated demand spikes, and δ(q2, S)=q2 for repeated solar tokens. Final state q2 ∈ F.

scenarios.title: Quiescent Baseline (Empty Sequence w = ε)
scenarios.description: Evaluates the machine under zero external inputs (empty word ε).
scenarios.academic_justification: By formal definition, δ*(q0, ε) = q0. Since IDLE (q0) ∈ F, the empty sequence is accepted, representing a safe, unperturbed power-on standby state.

scenarios.title: Safety Alert During Active Load Curtailment
scenarios.description: Verifies that emergency fault handling operates unconditionally when the system is already under stress in ENERGY_SAVING mode.
scenarios.academic_justification: Direct trip δ(q3, A) = q4. Once in q4, solar input S cannot clear the fault. Sequence rejected (q4 ∉ F).

scenarios.title: Rejection of Out-of-Alphabet Malformed Inputs
scenarios.description: Validates parser robustness when corrupted or unrecognized telemetry tokens are presented.
scenarios.academic_justification: Formal language definition strictly rejects tokens σ ∉ Σ by raising InvalidSymbolError, preventing undefined non-deterministic behavior.
